title: Serialized environment promotions in a CI system
name: Environment promotion coordinator

locateQuestion.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code acquires and releases the per-environment lock? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
locateQuestion.explanation: The lock is released by hand on each expected path, but not in a finally block. If target.apply() rejects (or currentDigest()/healthCheck() throw), the exception leaves promote() with the lock still held. Every later promotion to that environment waits in acquire() forever, and status() keeps reporting the failed pipeline as the holder. Wrapping the work after acquire() in try/finally fixes it.

choiceQuestions.prompt: Two pipelines call promote("staging", ...) with different digests at nearly the same time. What happens?
choices: Both apply concurrently because each gets its own EnvironmentLock
The second throws immediately because the lock is held
The second waits until the first releases, then checks currentDigest() and deploys
The second is skipped because currentDigest() was read before the first finished
choiceQuestions.explanation: lockFor() returns the same EnvironmentLock per environment name, and acquire() parks the second caller in waiters until release() wakes it. It then reads currentDigest() under the lock, sees the first pipeline's digest, and deploys its own. It does not throw, and the digest read happens after waiting, not before.

choiceQuestions.prompt: Why does EnvironmentLock.acquire() re-check `this.held` in a while loop after being woken instead of just taking the lock?
choices: Because release() wakes every waiter at once
Because another caller can call acquire() and take the lock between the wake-up and the woken waiter resuming
Because Promises can resolve more than once
It is unnecessary; an if statement would behave identically in every case
choiceQuestions.explanation: release() resolves the next waiter, but that waiter only resumes on a later microtask. A brand-new acquire() call running in between sees held === false and takes the lock, so the woken waiter must check again. release() wakes only one waiter, and promises resolve once.

choiceQuestions.prompt: A pipeline re-promotes a digest that is already live in production. What does promote() do?
choices: Re-applies it and runs the health check again
Returns skipped: true without ever touching the lock
Returns skipped: true without calling apply(), after acquiring and releasing the lock
choiceQuestions.explanation: The digest comparison happens after acquire(), so it reflects the state under the lock; on a match it releases and returns skipped: true without apply() or healthCheck(). Nothing throws, and the lock is taken first.
